title: Support for Custom Headers in OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow
body:
In the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow, certain Identity Providers like Microsoft require specific headers during the access token call. Without these headers, requests fail with errors like AADSTS9002327: Tokens issued for the 'Single-Page Application' client-type may only be redeemed via cross-origin requests.

Developers should be able to include custom headers, such as Origin, when making the access token call, ensuring seamless integration with Identity Providers that require specific headers.

title: BUG: OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow fails for intermediate redirects
body:
The authorization process will fail for authorization servers offering a "multi-step" authorization that include intemediate redirects casually containing the keyword `code` in their uri.

I happen to use an authorization server that guides the user through several forms (connected through intemediate redirects) during the authorization process. One of the intermediate redirect casually contains `code` in the uri (but not as the distinct query parameter). Thus the authorization code flow fails with the following error trace:

```
Error occurred in handler for 'send-http-request': Error: Invalid Callback Url
    at onWindowRedirect (~/devel/bruno/packages/bruno-electron/out/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/src/ipc/network/authorize-user-in-window.js:30:18)
    at EventEmitter.didNavigateListener (~/devel/bruno/packages/bruno-electron/out/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/src/ipc/network/authorize-user-in-window.js:67:7)
    at EventEmitter.emit (node:events:527:28)
```

title: Check oauth2 authorization code redirect for exact 'code' query parameter
body:
# Description

Redirects during OAuth2 authorization code flow are only identified through a rather broad regex match for `code` in the redirect uri. The authorization process will fail for authorization servers offering a "multi-step" authorization that include intemediate redirects casually containing the keyword `code` in their uri.

This change checks the redirect for the distinct `code` query paramter [as defined in the RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.2)

title: [Feature Request] Path parameter support (ex `/customer/:id`)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

body:
Postman supports setting path parameters using a `:value` syntax. See https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/create-requests/parameters/#send-request-parameters
> Path parameters form part of the request URL, and are referenced using placeholders preceded by `:` as in the following example: `/customer/:id`

I've used these _extensively_ in Postman which is making my switch to using Bruno quite difficult.

Please add support for these path variables to Bruno.

title: [Bug] Using a `/` in an Environment Name causes error
body:
I ran into this while attempting to import a Postman Environment. I had an environment I called "Beta / Staging" in Postman which would result in an `An error occurred while importing the environment`. After some experimenting with the json I removed the `/` character and it imported fine.

To reproduce:
1. Click `Configure` for the environments
2. Click `+ Create`
3. Set the Environment Name to `Some / Thing` (any name which includes a `/` will cause the error)
4. Click the `Create` button
5. Note the error `An error occurred while created the environment` is displayed

Setting the environment to include other special characters such as `~` or `=` or even `\` works fine. It only appears to happen with `/`.

I tried looking in the developer console and I don't see any errors showing up there. I'm not sure where to go looking for generated log files that might give additional details on the actual error root cause.

title: Support disabling the tab bar
body:
For users who like the Insomnia UI model more than the Postman UI model, add an option to disable tabs completely.

### Rationale

One thing I **loved** in Insomnia is that it did not copy Postman's messy tab UI. Instead, you just have a bunch of requests in your sidebar, neatly organized into groups. You pick one and run it. You edit it, it is automatically saved (#1679). You switch to another request, then to another. No tabs to close, nothing to manage.

In contrast, the tabs that Postman and Bruno currently implement have an inherent cost:

- Looking around, reading and running a few requests, maybe making changes to a few of them accumulates tabs, more tabs and even more tabs. This produces clutter in the UI, and the user has to use mental capacity to manage and navigate these tabs

What's worse, these tabs IMO do not add valuable functionality. They are not needed, as everything they do can (could) be done equally well by the sidebar:

- Once I have selected a request, it no longer matters what request I had selected before that. If I want to switch back to that other request, I will just click it in the side bar.
- As the ordering of the requests in the sidebar is persistent and stable, I tend to remember where I placed some request. I might even put a few requests I use often into a designated group. Tabs, on the other hand, just appear in the order I opened them today.
- The "unsaved" indicator on the tab could just as easily be placed on the request name in the sidebar. Also, if requests are saved automatically like in Insomnia (#1679), there is no "unsaved" indicator anymore.

title: Importing without selecting a location doesn't show an error
body:
### Problem
After I selected an Insomnia file for importing, a dialog appeared that displayed the name of the collection and a box labelled "Location" with a "Browse" link beneath. I suspected the latter would be needed so that Bruno knows where to store the newly created .bru files, but I wasn't entirely sure. So I decided to just leave it empty and clicked the "Import" button.

Bruno said the import was successful, but nothing else happened:
- the new collection did not appear in the sidebar
- If Bruno created any .bru files anywhere on my disk, I didn't find them. (I checked the directory of the import file and the Bruno program directory.)

When I repeated the process and selected a location, everything worked as expected.

### Suggestion
The location field should be clearly marked as being required and the "Import" button should be grayed out until a location was selected.

### Notes
Tested with Bruno v1.10.0 on Windows.

title: [Bug] JSON numerics longer than 16 digits are transformed to a different value
body:
## Summary ##
When processing JSON bodies, Bruno transforms numeric values longer than 16 digits in length, resulting in incorrect data passing to the target endpoint.

## Reproduction ##
This is quite easy to reproduce in two ways.

**Method 1**
Create a JSON POST request with the following body:
``` JSON
[
  {
    "id": 1234567890123456,
    "index": 1
  },
  {
    "id": 12345678901234567,
    "index": 2
  },
  {
    "id": 123456789012345678,
    "index": 3
  },
  {
    "id": 1234567890123456789,
    "index": 4
  },
  {
    "id": 12345678901234567890,
    "index": 5
  }
]
````

Notice that item 1 (index 1) has a 16 digit ID and that all subsequent items have one more digit than the previous. 

Click "Timeline" in Bruno and then execute the request. After executing the request, review the payload "data" in the "Timeline" pane and note that Bruno modified all digits after the 16th place in the IDs. This results in incorrect IDs being passed to the endpoint.

Here's a screenshot of the behavior:

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/60630345/92725075-ec79-4209-a3bb-2540da81f822)

**Method 2**
With the same JSON listed in method 1 still in the "Body", simply hit the "Prettify" button. This will update the request with the same morphed values seen above.

Here are before and after screenshots, illustrating the bug:

Before hitting "Prettify"
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/60630345/cfe3b103-d568-452a-bfa7-265b109dbca7)

After hitting "Prettify"
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/60630345/bcb04265-dd78-4931-95cd-92b9e6478e51)

I realize that this is most likely caused by limitations of  JSON.parse() and that it rounds large numbers. I also realize that it can technically be avoided by wrapping the numbers in quotes and treating them like strings, but doing that feels dirty and puts a burden on users to transform JSON they might be pasting in from their system etc. I have confirmed that this is not a problem in Postman or Insomnia so it may be worth considering.

title: CLI: `query` declaration ignored
[Bug] `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` headers break response
body:
When response has both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers, Bruno fails to show response.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Call endpoint that returns both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers.

### Expected behavior
* Show response body
* Warn user about conflicting headers received

### Actual behavior
* No response body, error is shown:
> Error invoking remote method 'send-http-request': Error: Parse Error: Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/20819782/cee8fe2c-0ba7-4bb7-a63e-6b6fc83d6249)


### Justificaiton
Standard requires us to ignore Content-Length in case of non-identity Transfer-Encoding, like "chunked", "compress", "deflate", or "gzip":
> "Messages MUST NOT include both a Content-Length header field and a non-identity transfer-coding. If the message does include a non-identity transfer-coding, the Content-Length MUST be ignored." ([RFC 2616, Section 4.4, point 3](http://greenbytes.de/tech/webdav/rfc2616.html#rfc.section.4.4))

(c) https://stackoverflow.com/a/3304186

UPD: [new RFC removed the part about ignoring](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230#section-3.3.2), though it would be great to warn user in this case, it might simplify troubleshooting.

title: `request-start-time` header results in HTTP 400
body:
Hi,

I'm currently migrating from postman to bruno and identified an issues with one of our internal apis.
I'm not owning this api and have no access to their code, but based on what I can see, it seems they have a strict header check.



While running the exact request in postman, I get a HTTP 200 response from the api.
Running the request in bruno results in a HTTP 400 with the error message like

```
request-start-time is not an allowed parameter for function....
```

After re-checking that it's not just "user handling", I searched for `request-start-time` in the bruno repo.

* https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Ausebruno%2Fbruno+request-start-time&type=code 

Based on the found results, the `request-start-time` header is used for measuring the time, so I would assume that we can't disable it.

* Any thoughts / ideas / workaround to solve this issue?
* Is this a bug or a "works as designed/expected"?

Note: It's just one API which has this behavior - everything is working and I'm soooooo excited to test the OAuth APIs in the next days ( hopefully ;) )

Thanks!

title: fix(#1518) Add support for displaying the response data in the Timeline and improve scripting error handling
body:
Closes #1518

# Description

Considering the following valid request which contains a scripting error:
```
meta {
  name: HttpBin
  type: http
  seq: 2
}

post {
  url: https://httpbin.org/post
  body: json
  auth: none
}

body:json {
  {  
      "test": "hello Bruno"  
  }  
}

vars:post-response {
  unknown_field: res.body.arguments.unknown_field
}
```

Bruno 1.9 and prior is showing the following response and timeline
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/15845066/71fd1f1e-07cc-4946-9984-73e982ada646)
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/15845066/38d8bad7-26a5-4353-9794-c6b552f2b374)

Whereas the request has been executed successfully the message is not really self explanatory and is hard for the user to understand. In fact a scripting error occured and **the user has no way to check to the root cause of the scripting error as the response is nowhere to be seen**.

This PR improves error handling during requests execution so that:
- Nothing is changed when a network error occurs while executing a request
- The error message displayed in the response pane is improved when a scripting error is raised during pre, post and testing phases
- A scripting error is not anymore considered as fatal (except for pre-request scripting errors) and the response is being returned to the renderer process
- The full response body is now logged into the timeline
- Errors are also being displayed in the timeline for easing debugging

For example, the request above is now displayed as following in the timeline:
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/15845066/c6fd449c-f6b2-4b5f-87e6-35678479e9d2)

To limit the potentials lags induced by logging large requests payloads in case of errors, three new user preferences have been introduced :
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/15845066/89b052bf-098a-4e30-a583-3b2126fe9333)

- Display the response in the timeline tab (Yes/No)
- Limit the display to responses which size is lower than the provided threshold (if the user specifies 0 then the setting is ignored and all sizes are considered)
- Limit the display to responses of the corresponding content types, if empty or '*' all the content types will be displayed

title: Bruno won't send ndjson body properly
body:
## Context
In Elasticsearch, when you want to do a [bulk indexing](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/docs-bulk.html), you send all documents in JSON separated by new lines (known as [ndjson](https://github.com/ndjson/ndjson-spec) or jsonl format). According to standard and Elasticsearch, body should end with a new line.

## Problem
In Bruno, it seems there's no way to send a body that ends with a new line, I tried JSON format or text, it doesn't matter. Seems somehow newline is removed somewhere. When I use "generate code" and copy the curl it's fine but when I run it in bruno Elasticsearch complains.

Sample .bru file:
```
meta {
  name: Bulk add 22
  type: http
  seq: 47
}

post {
  url: {{ES_URL}}/tmp/_bulk
  body: json
  auth: none
}

headers {
  Content-Type: application/json
}

body:json {
  { "update" : {"_id" : "6"}
  { "doc" : {"f1" : 8}, "doc_as_upsert" : true}

}
```

Sample cURL:
```shell
curl --request POST \
  --url http://localhost:9200/tmp/_bulk \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{ "update" : {"_id" : "6"}
{ "doc" : {"f1" : 8}, "doc_as_upsert" : true}
'
```

Error returned from Elasticsearch (only when run with bru):
```json
{
  "error": {
    "root_cause": [
      {
        "type": "illegal_argument_exception",
        "reason": "The bulk request must be terminated by a newline [\\n]"
      }
    ],
    "type": "illegal_argument_exception",
    "reason": "The bulk request must be terminated by a newline [\\n]"
  },
  "status": 400
}
```

When I run an nc on my local, I get a weird body being sent:
```
➜  ~ nc -l 9200
POST /tmp/_bulk HTTP/1.1
Accept: application/json, text/plain, */*
Content-Type: application/json
request-start-time: 1708628407192
User-Agent: axios/1.5.1
Content-Length: 93
Accept-Encoding: gzip, compress, deflate, br
Host: localhost:9200
Connection: close

"{ \"update\" : {\"_id\" : \"6\"}\n{ \"doc\" : {\"f1\" : 8}, \"doc_as_upsert\" : true}\n\n\n"
```


BTW keep up good work 🙌 I'm waiting for my golden edition ☺️

title: [Feature] Import HTTP Archives (HAR)
body:
HTTP Archives are the standard and open way to store a web session history. Importing a complete session is very helpful. It is a fairly simple format: https://w3c.github.io/web-performance/specs/HAR/Overview.html

- Insomnia already supports this https://docs.insomnia.rest/insomnia/import-export-data 
- Hopscotch has an open issue: https://github.com/hoppscotch/hoppscotch/issues/2409
- Firecamp is working on it: https://github.com/firecamp-dev/firecamp/issues/146
- Postman supports it as well: https://blog.postman.com/postman-now-supports-importing-har-files/

Since various other tools also support HAR exports, it would provide a common interop layer that would make issues like #1629 easier to solve.

title: fix(#1491) Cloning item drafts before saving in exit app flow
body:
# Description (longer than the correction)

I replayed exactly the scenario described by the issue author in [this comment](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/1491#issuecomment-1943572861) and tracked the issue to a mutation that happens during the `saveMultipleRequests` action, throwing an error: 

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/5250902/166f0619-80e1-4bd9-b544-c4f25ad3e928)

As explained [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Errors/Cant_define_property_object_not_extensible) this should originate if the object being mutated explicitly has a protection against adding new properties. I never encountered this before, but maybe it's something [by design of react-redux](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74460797/redux-object-object-is-not-extensible-error-when-creating-new-attribute-for-arra)?

Inspecting the objects during debug it seems to be the case:
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/5250902/343a9f2b-6123-46de-99cd-7de7d21f0db3)

This problem doesn't happen when closing just the tab, which uses the `saveRequest` action instead. There the collection and the tab are cloned before entering `transformRequestToSaveToFilesystem` function, which avoids any mutation protections. 
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/5250902/c663a325-5458-421f-9c4f-b60af19f8b9f)

Applying the same for `saveMultipleRequests` solved the issue.

title: [Bug] collection.bru considered as a regular request by bruno CLI
body:
*I'm reposting this, as I'm afraid it will be very hard to find digged in comments.*

This happens on latest bruno CLI 1.9.0. Also happening in previous versions, down to 1.3.0.

Hi, I have been experimenting with collection pre-request and post-response scripts to have a cookie being picked up when running `bru run`, but I keep getting an error when running the collection:

```
Running Folder 

collection (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND undefined)   <-- error here
1-setcookie (200 OK) - 279 ms
manually saving the cookie
2-getcookie (200 OK) - 137 ms

Requests:    2 passed, 1 failed, 3 total
Tests:       0 passed, 0 total
Assertions:  0 passed, 0 total
```

It looks like collection.bru is mistakenly being picked up as a runnable request, which in turn has no URL, resulting in the host being `undefined`.

The `collection.bru` file looks like this:

```
script:pre-request {
  if (bru.getVar("THE_COOKIE")) {
      req.setHeader("Cookie", bru.getVar("THE_COOKIE"));  
  }
}

script:post-response {
  const cookie = res.getHeader("set-cookie");
  if (cookie) {
      console.log("manualing saving the cookie");
      bru.setVar("THE_COOKIE", cookie);  
  }
}
```

Basically, the scripts in the post-response looks for a `Set-Cookie` header, and it stores it in the collection variable `THE_COOKIE`. For every subsequent request, if the collection var is set, it adds a `Cookie` header with its value.

[Here attached](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/files/14086990/integration-general.zip) is a Proof of Concept to help reproduce the issue. 

To reproduce this:

```sh
$ cd dev-integration/
$ npm install
$ npx bru run .

Running Folder 

collection (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND undefined) 
1-setcookie (200 OK) - 279 ms
manually saving the cookie
2-getcookie (200 OK) - 137 ms

Requests:    2 passed, 1 failed, 3 total
Tests:       0 passed, 0 total
Assertions:  0 passed, 0 total
```

I expected `Requests: 2 passed, 0 failed, 2 total`, but maybe I'm doing something wrong myself 👀

_Originally posted by @Giako in https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/334#issuecomment-1915096021_

title: Multi-part requests: user should be able to set content-type for each part in a multi-part request.
body:
When setting up a multipart request, Bruno automatically selects the content-type of the file part. The auto-assigned content-type is not always the desired content-type of the API spec, therefore our request will always result in a 400 Bad Request, because the content-type is wrong.

**Please allow a way for the user to set the content type for a multi-part request part. File or text**

**Text/Param:** user should be able to set because this could be blank, application/json, application/xml, text/plain or many other things.
**Files:** user should be able to set because this could be blank, application/pdf, application/octet-stream, application/vnd.ms-excel, text/csv or many other things.

Example: Multipart Form Data: PDF file content-type automatically set. No manual way for user to set content-type for a file.
Why is this a problem: API spec for the pdf file wants "application/octet-stream" for the content-type. Bruno automatically sets the content-type to "application/pdf". No way to manually set the content-type. Results in 400 bad request because content-type does not match API spec and there is no way to change in Bruno.

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/131696171/66d14d8c-6125-4f8e-a22e-23e373d1de9f)

This appears to align with your plans to update the Bru Lang Schema https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/1502 but I want to make sure the user can set the content-type in the UI for params and files.

## Versions
v1.9.0


## Steps to reproduce 1
1. Create POST request
2. Go to Body 
3. Select Multipart Form
4. Click Add Param
5. Enter key and value <---User cannot change content-type of the file

## Steps to reproduce 2
1. Create POST request
2. Go to Body 
3. Select Multipart Form
4. Click Add File
5. Enter key and select file<---User cannot change content-type of the file


For reference this is how it works in Postman:
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/131696171/2eb231ad-7de5-40e8-a5fa-31b01d2a3b24)

title: Newline in environment variable value does not save unless you mark it as a secret
body:
1. Go to configure your environments.
2. Select an environment
3. Add a new variable, setting a name
4. Now add a multiline value such as a public key, or really anything (e.g. `line 1\nline 2`--actually use a new line, not a `\n`)
5. Hit save
6. Close and reopen the environment
7. The variable isn't there!
8. Now repeat the same steps 1-4 and then mark the variable as a secret
9. Repeat steps 5-6
10. The variable is there!

## Issue
Newline in environment variable value does not save unless you mark it as a secret

## Impact
Low because of the workaround

## Workaround
Check "secret" so that it can save -- not always possible depending on if you want to share this as a collection with the newline

```
my-collection/
├─ my-request.bru
├─ my-file.pdf
```

title: Collection specifying Basic Auth is not overwritten when Request specifies Bearer Token

Te expected behaviour is for the Request configuration to **always** take precedence over Collection configurations that are set as default fallbacks.

title: feat(#1496) Allow ignoring path fragments from the collection configuration file
body:
# Description

This PR resolves #1496 by enhancing the `bruno.json` collection configuration file with a new property named `ignore` allowing to specify a list of path fragments which should be excluded when loading a collection.

For instance :
```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "name": "Sample Collection",
  "type": "collection",
  "ignore": [
  	".idea",
  	".vscode",
        "Test/Test2"
  ]
}
```

Collection creation behavior has also been updated so that default exclusions initially handled in the code (_node_modules, .git_ folders) are now written by default in the collection configuration file.

Opening legacy collections will work as expected as default exclusions will be applied if no exclusion configuration can be found.

The collection info tab has been updated in order to display the list of excluded path items

## Expected Behavior
When displaying data in the Response window, all characters should show as proper characters.

title: [Feature Request] support recursive traversal for `.bru` files
body:
At the moment Bruno expect to have a folder where every route is.

In our project we don't group by kind of file (eg: docs, controller, model, hook, view) but by context. The idea is to co-locate `.bru` files with other sources, like the HTTP route that define the endpoint. 

Another point is, when using VSCode, we can use capture patterns and group `.bru` files with other sources:
```
└── MyUseCase
    ├── MyEndpoint.ts
    ├── MyEndpoint.bru
    ├── MyEndpoint.md
    └── MyEndpoint.spec.ts
```

Traversing recursively the collection folder, would unlock this possibility being backward compatible with old version.

title: feat: improve DX with new dev command and updated contribution guidelines
body:
# Description

## TLDR

This
```
npm run build:graphql-docs
npm run build:bruno-query
npm run build:bruno-common

# terminal 1
npm run dev:web

# terminal 2
npm run dev:electron
```

is replaced with this
```
npm run dev
```

Currently, there are some manual steps included to run the app locally, which includes building all packages locally and then run `next` and `electron` in two separate terminals. This is a bit cumbersome and we also lose the hot reload for the packages that are built beforehand.

title: "Add" cookies feature. Support for cookie propagation in case if target page returns 302.
body:
Related to:
https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/968

If we have a chain of requests, i.e: request -> 302 re-direct -> 302 re-direct -> page.
Cookies from the first re-direct response are not propagated further.
This happens because of the way how axios works:
https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/3862

Solution:
During the request preparation, if "Save cookies" checkbox is set, maxRedirections for axios instance will be set to 0 and further re-direction requests will be triggered re-cursively in error handler, new interceptors will be storing and enriching cookies.

Cookies UI:
New element allowing manual addition of the cookies is implemented. Table key is changed from domain to domain + path.

title: String Interpolation
body:
String Interpolation

### Goal
Today our interpolation logic is duplicated across multiple packages (App, Electron, CLI)
The goal is to centralize a single source of truth for all interpolation logic.

### Considerations
* We want to be flexible in terms of key naming conventions
  * #931 
  * #964 
* We plan to support Nested environments in the future
  * #292 
  * #1098

### Moving away from handlebars
I think its time to move away from handlebars.
We don't need the full power of handlebars and we want write a custom interpolation function that meets our needs instead of shoehorning handlebars to match our use case.

### Related Tickets

title: Is there a way to store secret values outside of environment variables?
body:
Hey all, first of all, love Bruno and I really hope it starts taking off to become a true Postman replacement, what they've done is an absolute slap in the face for open source.

title: ECONNREFUSED error when using localhost with proxy endpoints
body:
I'm running and testing a local proxy server meant to function as an API gateway. It is built in nodejs [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) v4.18.2 and [http-proxy-middleware](https://github.com/chimurai/http-proxy-middleware) v2.0.6, and is currently as simple as possible. 

* One path `'/hello'` returns "Hello" text.
* Another path `'/auth'` is set up as a proxy with a `target` URL out on the internet (a server I manage) and `changeOrigin` set to `true`.
* Another path `'/dog'` is also a proxy with a target to this public API: https://dog.ceo/api/breeds/image/random

When hitting the proxied `auth` endpoint I'm seeing this error:

```
Error invoking remote method 'send-http-request': Error: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:443
```

Related to https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/124 but obviously different.

# Details

- Windows 10
- Bruno desktop app v1.6.1

# Tests

- ✅✅ When requesting a URL in Bruno that is not proxied, e.g., `http://localhost:3201/hello` just returns text, I get the response expected. This also works as expected in Postman and the browser (Chrome 120.0.6099.225).
- ❌ When requesting a URL in Bruno that *is* proxied, e.g., `http://localhost:3201/auth` I get the error above.
- ✅ When requesting the same `'/auth'` proxied URL in either Postman or the browser, I get the response I would expect (which in my case is a JSON object from the proxied API saying the authentication didn't work because I'm doing a GET and not sending any data).
- ✅✅ When requesting "http://localhost:3201/dog" in either Bruno, Postman, or the browser, they all work as expected.

Since the "dog" endpoint works, but "auth" does not, I admit there is likely something unusual happening with my target server. But it is disconcerting that Bruno acts different from Postman and the browser.

title: FIX: Request>Auth>Bearer configuration does not override if Collection>Auth>Basic is set.
body:
# Description

Fixes https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/1536 and https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/960

The way axios handles the `auth` property on the request configurations makes it such that it will always take precedence over the `headers.authorization` for the headers object. This was causing issues where the Bruno Collection has Basic Auth and the Request being run has Bearer Auth.

## Reproducing

1. In Collection>Settings>Auth select Basic
2. In a Request>Auth select Bearer
3. Spin up an http server; preferably with a debugger and a breakpoint on the endpoint
4. Inspect the `req.headers` property the server received

This will result in `Basic ========`; in this fix it should be `Bearer =======`

## Alternative implementation

Instead of inverting logic and doing conditional validations consider potentially mutating the request object.
By doing `delete request.auth` on the condition for the request on bearer mode the bug can be avoided. Although I tend to shy away from mutating objects this way as it may have unintended side-effects.

title: Add ability to paginate
body:
## Problem
Some endpoints will limit the amount of data in the response and expect another request (i.e. paginate) to get additional data

## Potential Solution
Provide the ability (or documentation if it already exists and I'm missing something!) to paginate with info from the previous response. This would mean that you would be able to set some variables to instruct Bruno if it should send another request and with what params.

e.g. 
request1: `{starting_id: undefined}`
response1: `{has_more: true, next_id: 11}`

Because `has_more` is true we can tell Bruno to automatically fire off another request and update the params:

request2: `{starting_id: 11}`
response2: `{has_more: false}`

Loving Bruno and thanks for taking this into consideration!

title: [BUG] Bruno Client Fails to Auto-Switch Response Format from Raw to Preview on text/html Content Type
body:
### Description
We are experiencing an issue with the Bruno client where the response format does not automatically switch from Raw to Preview when the content type is changed to `text/html`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Send a GET request that returns a JSON response. The response is correctly formatted in JSON.
2. Update the server-side code to modify the endpoint to return a different content type, specifically text/html (e.g., using the `dd()` function in Laravel).
3. Resend the GET request. The response is expected to switch to `Preview` format in Bruno, but it continues to be formatted as `Raw`.

### Expected Behavior
Upon modifying the server-side endpoint to return `text/html`, the Bruno client is expected to mirror the behavior of clients like Insomnia or Postman, automatically transitioning the response format from Raw to Preview in alignment with the specified content type.

### Current Behavior
After changing the server-side endpoint to return `text/html`, the response in Bruno unexpectedly remains in `Raw` format. This requires manual switching to 'Raw' format in Bruno, which is counterintuitive and disregards the custom rules set for these content types.

title: Bruno parses incorrectly URL used to make ServiceNow JSON API request
body:
Discovered issue while using the ServiceNow JSONv2 API ([link](https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/tokyo-application-development/page/integrate/inbound-other-web-services/concept/c_DataModificationAPI.html))

In short, bruno does not parse correctly request URLs that have empty Query params or params whose value look like Query params. For instance, the following URL is used in ServiceNow to update a ticket whose number us INC00123. 

https://your_instance.service-now.com/incident.do?JSONv2&sysparm_action=update&sysparm_query=number=INC00123

 If I add that URL to bruno and then save the request or add a new 'Query' param, bruno will try to parse the URL and it will not parse the  'sysparm_query=number=INC00123' section of the URL correctly. It will also add 'JSONv2' as an empty param, which is expected, but it will then remove that param from the request URL any time it tries to re-parse the URL (see screenshots)

body:
### Description

I am currently using version 1.6.1 on MacOS. I have encountered a bug where attempting to name a REQUEST with any name starting with "/" results in the following error:

```
Error invoking remote method 'renderer:new-request': Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Users/**/Desktop/collections/My Collection/My Folder//auth/sign-in/lookup.bru'
```

I've identified that the method used to create the file path is concatenating the literal name I provided with the relative project path. It seems that there is an issue with the concatenation process, leading to the creation of an incorrect file path.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Attempt to create "New Request" or "Rename" existing request
2. Enter a name for the request that starts with "/" (e.g., "/example").

### Expected Behavior

Creating a request with a name starting with "/" should not result in a file path error.

title: [Feature] Prompt user to save requests before exiting app
body:
# Description

[Screencast from 2024-01-04 00-21-24.webm](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/5250902/a0bad655-f3b3-458f-8e59-2cf569002140)

## Concept
- This PR introduces the behavior in which the app, before quitting, checks for any unsaved requests changed by the user and prompts them to save or discard each one.
- Inspired by `useCollectionNextAction` hook, I introduced an event queue to be able to handle the sequence of steps involved in this.
- This queue is managed by [listener middleware](https://redux-toolkit.js.org/api/createListenerMiddleware) of React Toolkit.
- Any change to the queue triggers a listener which picks the first event and dispatches one action in response to it.
- Other listeners were setup tracking actions that "complete" each event type. If confirmed that the action handles the first event from queue, it removes this event and prompts the queue listener to process the next event, and so on.

## Event types

- `OPEN_REQUEST`: it focus or add a new tab for an item. The event is completed by the same actions it trigger (`addTab` and `focusTab`).
- `CLOSE_REQUEST`: it opens the confirmation modal for an unsaved request or just closes the request. The event is completed by the action closing the tab (`closeTabs`).
- `CLOSE_APP`: it closes the main window and quits Bruno.

## Application

- The chain of prompts before quitting is implemented as a chain of `OPEN_REQUEST` AND `CLOSE_REQUEST` events and a `CLOSE_APP` at the end. If the user cancels any of the prompts (clicking in the "X" icon), the rest of the events is also aborted.
- I used an `OPEN_REQUEST` event to implement the behavior of opening the request just after creating it (replacing `useCollectionNextAction`).

## Additional Changes

- Added the request name to the confirmation modal message. It seemed useful when being prompted several times.
- I noticed some unimplemented props that were being passed to the `Modal` component in `ConfirmRequestClose`: `disableEscapeKey` and `disableCloseOnOutsideClick`. I tried an implementation for them and they seem to work as intended. The user explicitly needs to click one of the buttons (or the "X" icon) to handle the `ConfirmRequestClose` modal. It can't be dismissed by mistake anymore.

## Bonus

- One capability of the listener middleware that I've found very useful for debugging purposes is logging every change in the Redux store declaring a listener like this:
```js
listenerMiddleware.startListening({
  predicate: () => true, // it'll track every change
  effect: (action, listenerApi) => {
    console.log('action', action.type); // which action did it
    console.log('action.payload', action.payload);
    console.log(listenerApi.getState()); // the updated store
  }
});
```

title: Feature/cli timeouts
body:
# Description

This PR implements setting & respecting timeouts in collection + request settings (resolves #1249). Prior to this PR, there is support for setting a single timeout value in the GUI, which is respected by the app when running requests. This PR implements:

1. Added UI for setting timeouts on the collection & individual requests, when there is collection + request setting, the request setting for timeout takes precedence
2. Existing timeout option in the Bruno app settings is used when collection & request doesn't have a timeout specified (it's a fallback)
3. CLI has a --timeout option which will take precedence over collection + request timeout options (when set)
4. CLI + GUI take into account timeout options when setting up requests, exceeding the timeout results in an axios timeout exception being raised in GUI / cli output

One pretty opinionated change that I made here was that I created a new "Meta" tab in the settings, and moved the Docs setting for collections + requests under it, and then added the new timeout option input underneath of Docs. I'm open to changing how this works or changing the name of it, but I think it may become useful to have a "miscellaneous settings" box for other settings that may be added to Bruno in the future anyways. It didn't seem like a good idea to add a tab just for timeouts, but if there's other ideas / name changes happy to make them.

title: TOML Support
body:
### Overview
This discussion aims to explore the possibility of using `.toml` as the preferred format for saving API request data instead of `.bru`. For the progression of the Domain-Specific Language (DSL), see https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/discussions/360

I've been seriously exploring how we can represent api requests in `toml`
After careful consideration, factoring in various edge cases, `toml` seems to fulfil our requirements and might offer better long-term benefits.

### Why TOML
- Well established format
- Utilize syntax highlighting in IDEs
- Leverage existing tooling for toml file manipulation
- Git providers (like GitHub, Bitbucket) offer syntax highlighting while reviewing pull requests on the web

### Tasks
 - [ ] Experimental support for working with TOML in GUI
 - [ ] Experimental support for working with TOML in CLI
 - [ ] Gather Community feedback during our community call on Wed Jan 3rd 2024
 
More Tasks TBD based on how the experiment turns out


### Looming Issues
Several features are currently blocked due to limitations in the bru language. Some include:

1. Describing headers
2. Managing choices for query parameters
3. File upload capabilities
4. Storing multiple payloads within a single request

To address these limitations, I see two potential paths:
1. Enhance Bru Lang
2. Utilize TOML

### Next Steps
Before choosing a direction, I aim to implement experimental TOML support in our current app within the next 3-4 days (by January 1st, 2024). . BTW I am working on bruno [Full Time](https://www.usebruno.com/blog/bootstrapping) from Jan 1st :)

title: Parallel Requests
body: I'm currently working on a project that's an e-commerce platform. We are planning to add a credit-like feature, in which the user can add items to the cart, and at checkout, they can choose either 'pay-on-pick' or credit. This will generate a payment order that will be paid 15 days later. Every client has a maximum credit amount, and we realized that if two clients from the same store make a credit purchase at the same time, both orders go through. To test this, I need to literally send two requests at (kind of) the same time, with at most a 2 to 3-second span between them. There is no way to do this without scripts, and I'm not really good at bash scripting, so having it on Bruno would be (at least to me) a big and usefull experience

title: Variables and pre-request scripts in code snippets
body: This is my first time writing here, so first of all: great project, I am really enjoying Bruno recently! Keep up the good work! ✊ When exporting a code snippet from a request, it only contains "static" data for Query, Body and Headers. When using a variable in a Header, the code snippet contains only `{{variable_name}}` rather than the variable's value. Same thing happens when assembling the Body in the pre-request script. The code snippet then contains no body at all. I'm not sure if it's a bug or just not implemented yet, but I think it would be more beneficial if a request was processed when exporting a code snippet as it would be processed if the request was actually sent. Otherwise, there is a constant risk that a code snippet will not produce the same result as the request from which it was exported. In the worst case, no result at all or even a result that causes damage.

title: [Feature] More configurable request timeouts
body:
Previously there was some work done in #557 to add configuration for request timeouts, however, the code addressed only some of what was discussed in that issue. I think it would be nice to:


1. Add support to the .bru / collection.bru files to specify a timeout
2. Handle the timeout settings in the bruno CLI
3. Allow a `--timeout` override option on the CLI (useful for CI environments where you might have different timing parameters than in local dev, for instance)
4. Add UI support for setting these timeout values

I have code done for 1-3, wondering about the UI though. Maybe "timeout" could go under the Presets tab in collection settings? I'm not sure where a good place would be for this config in the request settings though. Vars might be the closest tab for something like this but even then it's not great, and adding another tab just for the timeout seems a little much. Any thoughts on what would make sense here? Is this feature useful? I could also punt on making the UI changes but I assume it's best to ship support for stuff like this with UI at the same time as it's enabled by the underlying system / config files. 

#557 also mentioned being able to configure this on the environment level, but I'm not sure how that would work because the environment configuration is all substitution variables, there's not something like a direct config override. Maybe that could work if the timeout settings in collection + request accepted variable substitution? Wondering if that's worth pursuing or not as well.

title: feat: OpenAPI import: create a default environment
body:
# Description

Fixes #1239

The previous solution constructed a default server baseUrl and directly concatenated it into each request of the collection. This makes it difficult to change it later through the UI if it is wrong or if the same OpenAPI spec can be used in multiple environments.

This solution instead creates a default environment with two variables "protocol" and "host", which are filled according to the previously constructed default baseUrl. This makes it very easy to change for all requests while preserving the server information extracted from the spec.

title: [docs] apt "Unable to locate package bruno"
body:
I'm writing a Dockerfile to install Bruno in a Debian container (because of #1030) but I get the following error on the `apt-get install bruno` instruction.

```
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree... Done
Reading state information... Done
E: Unable to locate package bruno
```

This is my Dockerfile:
```Dockerfile
FROM debian:11-slim

RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
  dumb-init \
  gpg \
  dirmngr \
  gpg-agent && \
  rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings 
RUN mkdir -m 700 -p /root/.gnupg
RUN gpg --no-default-keyring --keyring /etc/apt/keyrings/bruno.gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys 9FA6017ECABE0266 

RUN echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/bruno.gpg] http://debian.usebruno.com/ bruno stable" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/bruno.list 
 
RUN apt-get update 
RUN apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bruno
# RUN grep ^ /etc/apt/sources.list /etc/apt/sources.list.d/* 
CMD ["dumb-init", "tail", "-f", "/dev/null"] # Helps debugging because it starts the container
```

When I run

title: Feature/junit reporter
body:
# Description

This adds a new flag to bru run, the `--format` flag. It defaults to `"json"`, which is the current output file format, while also implementing a `"junit"` option that will produce JUnit-formatted XML.

There are some opinionated implementation choices which I don't have strong opinions about:

1. Using the bru filename (minus `.bru`) for test suite names in the junit markup
2. Using a structure where the filename becomes a JUnit test suite, and then assertions + tests become test cases inside the suite
3. JUnit tests (often? must?) supply a `time` attribute, and I had access to timing details on the .bru file / test suite level, but not the test case level. For implementation simplicity what I did was I used timing details from the .bru file to set the `time` attribute on the test suite, and then I divided it equally for the child testcases (which are the assertions / individual tests). This seemed accurate enough while hopefully not breaking some tooling that expects the `time` attr to be present

Also, I don't think I messed anything up applying a new npm module for xml writing (and chose a module which was already being required outside of the cli package), but the package-lock.json file updated widely so probably best to double-check there. I also removed a `@jest/globals` require in the test file because I couldn't get that to work locally, I can add that back, but I'm pretty sure it's unnecessary? And of course happy to address any feedback.

MOST IMPORTANTLY: THANK YOU so much for your work on Bruno, this project is awesome. I have now been burned twice on tools in this family (once with Swagger, and now again with Insomnia) adopting cloud policies that will never be acceptable as a business risk. I want to figure out how to champion sponsorship for this project but until then, consider this a small token of appreciation 😄

title: Feature Request: Script and tests at folder level
body:
It would be very useful if it is possible to execute scripts or tests at folder level.

My use case is that the service i am testing runs on a system where changes are applied very frequently. Therefore I have the demand to repeat all requests in a folder in case an error occurred. But because I can not execute at folder level I can only rerun the complete collection. this is frustrating because the collection needs one hour or more but the changes are applied ever five minutes.

If scripts and tests are available at folder level I can count errors an retries at this level. So I can decide where to skip using the new bru.setNextRequest feature.

title: [UX] Warn if there are unsaved requests when quitting Bruno
body:
Situation: I sometimes edit my requests but forget to save them. When I quit Bruno with cmd+q etc. my changes will be lost without a warning. I'm also mostly used to applications to just remember my input or at least ask for confirmation before continuing with a destructive operation.

I've lost my changes several times already and I think UX could be improved a lot here by simply warning the user before quitting when there are unsaved files.

For closing an unsaved tab this already is implemented. So this could probably be reused for the whole application as well.

title: Protocol parsing can be improved
body:
Currently protocols are parse as follows:
```javascript
const protocolRegex = /([a-zA-Z]{2,20}:\/\/)(.*)/;
```

While this regex is likely to work in the vast majority of situations, there are some where it may fail.  For example, protocols are allowed to contain a dash character (see [IANA URL schemes](https://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/uri-schemes.xhtml))

Since Bruno makes use of Axios, it makes sense to match the protocol parsing to [their library's protocol parsing](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/main/lib/helpers/parseProtocol.js) which is more precise.

```javascript
const protocolRegex = /^([-+\w]{1,25})(:?\/\/|:)/;
```

title: 1st occurrence of process.env.{{VARIABLE}} is not handled when used in Body
body: When using `{{process.env.VARIABLE}}` within the payload body to reference the `.env` secret variables, the first use does not populate. [Bruno v1.3.1] _cat .env_ ``` DOT_VAR1=fromDotFile ``` _Payload body_ ``` { "key0" : "Value0", "Key1" : "{{process.env.DOT_VAR1}}", "Key2" : "{{process.env.DOT_VAR1}}", "Key3" : "{{process.env.DOT_VAR1}}" } ``` _data passed to server_ ``` { "key0": "Value0", "Key1": "", "Key2": "fromDotFile", "Key3": "fromDotFile" } ``` If key1 is deleted from payload body, key2 is then blank on submit. It can worked around but using a pre-request script to set as collection variable and updating payload body variable. ``` bru.setVar("DOT_VAR1", bru.getProcessEnv("DOT_VAR1")); ```

title: [Feature Request] Multiline strings in Form URL Encoded bodies
body:
Some of our API endpoints require multiline strings of JSON or XML to be passed via URL parameters.  

Currently in Bruno the body parameter editor only allows you to see one line at a time. The user is still able to scroll through the data using the up and down arrow keys but it can be tedious. The .bru format will also convert these into an escaped single line string which also makes it difficult to work with.

### Current implementation
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/1078339/fbfaf332-2965-461b-9d16-19b9b327f411)

### Proposed Change

A potential format for multiline string values could be something like this, based on how script blocks are already handled in Bruno

```
body:form-urlencoded {
  Action: SendMessage
  MessageBody: {
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <TestEvent>
      <Name>Test</name>
      <Value>123</value>
    </TestEvent>
  }
}
```

The UI could take inspiration from Insomnia

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/1078339/77430021-db3f-46f9-a010-8d47c38dff45)

title: Docs editor font doesn't follow value set in Preferences.
body:
## Issue

The CodeMirror editor for the Docs tab in a request doesn't follow the font set in the preferences window.

## Fix

The fix for this issue is to pass the `font` property to the CodeMirror component. I have opened a PR that fixes this issue.

**Pull Request:** #1132 
**CodeMirror Component:** [/packages/bruno-app/src/components/CodeEditor/index.js](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/main/packages/bruno-app/src/components/CodeEditor/index.js)
**Problematic File:** [/packages/bruno-app/src/components/Documentation/index.js](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/main/packages/bruno-app/src/components/Documentation/index.js)

## Considerations

As far as I know, the ability to change the font for code editing in Bruno should apply to every instance of the CodeMirror component. Its possible that instead of passing the `font` property, we could instead get the font on the CodeMirror component itself.

This however has not been implemented in the pull request that I've linked above.

## Observations

### Expected

Bruno to use the font provided in the Preferences dialog to affect the Docs code editor.
In my case, my font is 0xProto (which is monospaced).

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/67294530/99963f31-b101-45c5-b2db-10fa8ac156d7)

### Actual

Bruno incorrectly disregards the font that the user has selected, and instead falls back to monospace.
My system does not have the monospace font installed, hence why the font instead falls back to Inter.

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/67294530/42b0656e-67a6-44fb-802a-ad502e3df880)

# Description

This PR fix #124, by correctly handling : 
- localhost subdomains (*.localhost) even if they are not inside a hosts file

This fix is heavily inspired by how PostmanRuntime is handling it (https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-runtime/blob/develop/lib/requester/core.js#L433),  their handling is even more complex by overriding DNS lookup of node (https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-runtime/blob/develop/lib/requester/core.js#L285).

I did some tests on windows & linux, and this PR correctly fix subdomains, or ipv6 issues.

title: [BUG] Vars in request override the environment variables definitely
body:
Hello, I am here to report a bug I found when starting to use bruno at work !

## Description of the issue

I create an environment variable, lets say `project_id` and set a value to the variable, for example `10`. I enable this environment and create a request that uses this env variable in its path. eg: `http://localhost:3000/projects/{{project_id}}/users`. When I run the request, everything works, the value `10` is reflected in the URL.

Then, I create a var of the same name in the Vars > Pre Request section. Lets says `project_id` with value `20`. When I send the request, now the value `20` is reflected in the URL as expected.

Then, I delete my Pre Request Variable and send the request again. **The value `20` is still reflected in the URL**. And the value will be reflected everywhere, even in other requests. This seems to indicate that the global state of the application has been affected by my request Vars. At this point, the only solution I found to reset my variable to its original value is to restart bruno completely.

## Expected behavior

As a user, I would expect that data specified in the Vars tab of one request should not affect the application global state, so that when I change requests or delete the Vars line, the behavior goes back to where it was before i created the Vars line.

## My 2 cents as a dev

I didn't take the time to take a look at bruno's source code, so I could be really wrong. This behavior gives the feeling that global state is used and modified while processing the request. This could become an issue in future developments, as it couples the action of sending the request with the use case (sending a request by clicking "send" in an item of a collection). This could make some future requests harder to implement (eg. creating a runner that sends multiple requests from a file) because you'll have to control and remember all the side effects to avoid unexpected behavior ! 

And thanks for all your work on bruno ! :)

title: Proposal: Conditional Workflow
body:
I am in the situation where I test an API against a service which is under development. A complete testrun will need about an hour. Therefore I am thinking about some scripts which are able to repeat some folder (all requests in the folder) as long as some error condition occur.

I have read https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/71 and https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/87 which go in my wanted direction. But both are missing the aspect of conditional execution an repetition of requests/folder. 

In postman which I want to discontinue there exists the command **postman.setNextRequest()** to implement some sort of workflow (Please see the [postman documentation](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collections/running-collections/building-workflows/)).

For example my collection looks like this:
```
Collection root
├── Folder: Create customer
│   ├── Request: Create customer
│   └── Request: Add address to customer
├── Folder: Create supplier
│   ├── Request: Create supplier
│   └── Request: Add address to supplier
└── Folder: Create contract
    ├── Request: Create contract
    ├── Request: Insert customer
    └── Request: Insert supplier

```

In this case I want to execute _Folder: Create customer_ three times. After three times and ending with a failing test the collection should be abborted completely. It does not make sense to create a contract, if there is no customer.

Then I want to execute _Folder: Create supplier_ three times. After three times and ending with a failing test the collection should be abborted completely. It does not make sense to create a contract, if there is no supplier.

Then I want to execute _Folder: Create contract_ three times. After three times and ending with a failing test the collection should be abborted completely. These repeatitions are only to make save, that the collection run successfully even if there are temporaly changes in the service I want to test.

I would like to nest variables inside other variables. So I can do a little bit of meta-programming to cleanup requests that typically use a lot of stuff that can be condensed into a single variable

For example
```
[Local Development]
protocol = "http"
host = "127.0.0.1"
user_service_port = "1111""
product_service_port = "2222"
user_service_url = "{{protocol}}://{{host}}:{{user_service_port}}
product_service_url = "{{protocol}}://{{host}}:{{product_service_port}}
```

```
[Staging Environment]
protocol = "https"
host = "some.staging.host"
user_service_port = "10111""
product_service_port = "20222"
user_service_url = "{{protocol}}://{{host}}:{{user_service_port}}
product_service_url = "{{protocol}}://{{host}}:{{product_service_port}}
```

Now in my requests, you can simply use `{{user_service_url}}/v1/version` instead of having to build the url in every request the same way, if you change the url scheme, you need to manually edit potentially a lot of end points.

I think this would be very useful.

title: [bug]: fix import aliases to avoid future import conflicts
body:
Alias imports use the following configuration : 
```json
"components/*": ["src/components/*"],
```
That means we import a button as
```jsx
import { Button } from "components/button"
```
Which might bring some import issues whenever we create a sub-directory named "components".
Same issue for assets, hooks, themes, api, pageComponents, providers and utils.
We should use the following syntax with a prefix to avoid conflicts : 
```json
"@components/*": ["src/components/*"],
```

title: Use system CA certificates and/or allow specifying additional CA certificates
body:
On a Mac, I try to access a resource that uses a custom CA certificate; it fails with:
```
Error invoking remote method 'send-http-request': Error: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```

I  already have that CA certificate in my keychain, so I can access corporate websites that use that CA certificate in a browser.

I am aware of the possibility to disable SSL verification, but don't like that idea. And neither do the security guys where I work.

I saw the issues https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/739 and https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/211 , which have a similar title and intention, but those people were satisfied when they discovered they could uncheck the SSL/TLS Certificate Validation checkbox.

Ideally, bruno would use the system CA certificates.

Insomnia has the same issue of not using the system certificates, but it allows specifying a CA certificate file to use. A solution like that would work for me too.

Is there by chance already some environment variable that I could use when launching bruno, so that it would look in a given file for certificates?  In https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/739, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` was mentioned (didn't work, apparently).

And thanks for bruno!

title: Undefined variables in request should not be replaced with empty strings
body:
When using strings surrounded with double braces, e.g. `{{some_content}}`, as part of the request, Bruno replaces them with empty strings before sending the request, if the content inside the braces is not a defined variable. Since this disables the user from sending such strings as part of the request, I propose that such unresolved variables should be sent verbatim as part of the request. This is the behavior in Postman as well.

### Reproduction
Use following cURL to reproduce this behavior:
```
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://webhook.site/d9fea9ac-2eb6-45b8-80e0-25f2a7030b20?q=-%3E%7B%7Bmy_q%7D%7D%3C-' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'my_header: ->{{my_header}}<-' \
  --data '{
  "name": "->{{my_name}}<-"
}'
```

![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/17818950/7f980a56-0a00-4f04-9cd6-ab5be4ea1201)

title: feat(#303): Default Environment
body:
Add environment to the presets tab which will set the default environment on opening a collection. Show default environment inside of environment selector. Also add cli support for default environments.

# Description
<!-- Explain here the changes your PR introduces and text to help us understand the context of this change. -->
This is to fix #303 by adding the property called `environment` inside of `Collection > Presets`. The collection descriptor file, `bruno.json` will now have the preset structure of:
```json
{
  "presets": {
     "defaultUrl": "",
     "defaultRequestType": "",
     "environment": null
  }
}
```
The preset environment will only change the environment under these conditions:
* The collection is first being opened
* The collection is being opened again and the current session had the environment set to `No Environment` (if its something else then it won't set the environment)

In the future we can rely on something like `lastEnvironment` to override the preset environment if people set it in their preferences.

https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/115114979/09145231-3f86-48be-9af7-0bf5e65df067

The environment selector now has a helpful indicator showing what the preset environment is by the yellow `(Default)` value at the end of it. Any old collections that don't have a preset environment or the environment can't be found in the current list of environments will default to `No Environment` insuring that nothing breaks. 

Some behavior that I need some guidance on @helloanoop, would be the formatting of `(Default)` indicator and whether to have it display next to `No Environment` if an environment preset is defined but not found. Currently I am setting it to `No Environment` in the environment selector and showing an error message on collection open when environment can't be found.

Now Bruno cli will try to look for the new `environment` preset value and set it as the environment if none is given.
![Default_Environment_cli](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/115114979/d6cef6a7-2a7a-47b4-8a37-5a52d404a2dc)

I think this is a very helpful QOL change that will make opening and testing APIs a quick and easy process.

title: [Bug] Empty variables shown as red in address bar
body:
## Problem:
An empty variable is shown as red in the address bar (indicating an error), but an empty variable can be intentional.

## How to reproduce:
1. in the environment, define two variables:
my-host=http://localhost:8080
my-base-path *leave empty*

2. in the address bar write {{my-host}}{{my-base-path}}/info

{{my-host}} will be highlighted green for 'works' and hovering the cursor over it will show the value.
{{my-base-path}} will be highlighted red for 'error' and hovering the cursor over it will not show the value.
The address will resolve correctly, so this is only a display issue.

## Context:
My service has a non-empty basepath when deployed, but when run locally the basepath is empty.
In Postman there was no such 'warning' when using empty variables.

## Proposed solution:
Since hovering over variables already shows their value, the appearing infobox should be warning enough to to user who might have left the value empty unintentionally. The infobox should either be empty, or show e.g. '\<empty\>' in italics to avoid confusing it with the possible value '\<empty\>'.

title: fix(#1012): silently ignore invalid cookie
body:
# Description

Closes #1012

After some digging, it looks like this is fixed by using the options `ignoreError`: `true` on [tough-cookie cookieJar.setCookieSync](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tough-cookie#setcookiecookieorstring-currenturl-options-callbackerr-cookie).

This will silently ignore many invalid cooke:
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/7304827/847550b6-b0ae-4035-a65a-8bae992577c7)


To validate the fix, I've added an endpoint in `bruno-testbench`:
```javascript
app.get('/cookies', function (req, res) {
  res.cookie('test-valid', 'something');
  res.cookie('test-invalid', 'something-invalid', { domain: 'invalid.com' });
  return res.send();
});
```
To keep the PR focused on the fix I have not included this but I'm happy to commit it if you prefer.

I've also tested the request in #1102 and the errors is indeed fixed.

title: [Feature Request] CLI For Converting OpenAPI 3 Spec to Bru
body:
Hello,

Our microservice platform team is currently in search of a new API Client App. We've found Bruno to be a promising candidate due to its filesystem-based approach.

Managing our 25+ microservices has proven to be a challenge with other popular API Client apps, particularly in keeping our local apps up-to-date. We believe that a CLI tool to convert our standard API specs into Bruno's format could be integrated into our CI/CD pipeline, significantly improving our workflow.

We propose the addition of a conversion/transformer command to the CLI. This command would take an OpenAPI spec as input, convert it into Bruno's format, and place the output in a specified directory.

We believe this feature would greatly enhance Bruno's usability, especially for teams managing a large number of microservices like ours.

Thank you for considering our proposal.

title: Fix package dependency issues in jsonlint
body:
We recently added json linting support in the codemirror editor - #925 #861

In order to get `jsonlint` to work, we had to install additional packages. - `file`, `system`
Also, the last package published was 6 years ago

Looking into its source code.
`require("file")` - https://github.com/zaach/jsonlint/blob/f6624322e6ba7c2c6e7848729f7309873329e7cb/lib/jsonlint.js#L424 
`require("system")` - https://github.com/zaach/jsonlint/blob/master/lib/jsonlint.js#L429-L431

At the very least, we need to raise a PR to `jsonlint` and have the dependencies in its package.json updated.
Or find another package that supports our needs.

Also, `jsonlint ` depends on `nomnom` which is deprecated

title: Lack of Multi-Part File Upload Support in Bruno HTTP Client
body:
## Description:
Currently, Bruno, our HTTP client, boasts impressive capabilities, but it falls short in a fundamental aspect: the ability to handle multi-part file uploads. This limitation hinders users from performing a basic task - sending files to the server. As a result, users are compelled to resort to alternative tools like Hoppscotch and Postman for this specific functionality.
> In bruno
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/32933220/9e161bd5-03fb-497a-92f1-25a604be7fd5)


## Request:
We propose the addition of support for multi-part file uploads in Bruno, enabling users to seamlessly send files to the backend. This enhancement would not only make Bruno a more comprehensive HTTP client but also position it as a viable alternative to existing tools like Postman.

> In postman
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/32933220/745364ae-1093-4298-97f9-a9df3d20fd5d)


## Impact:
The absence of this feature has led users to rely on other tools for file upload functionality, limiting Bruno's adoption as an all-in-one HTTP client solution. Addressing this issue would significantly enhance the user experience and broaden Bruno's utility, aligning it more closely with the expectations of users seeking a Postman alternative.

title: Large Postman Imports are Incomplete
body:
### What I was trying to do
Import a large Postman collection into Bruno

### What was supposed to happen
All folders and requests should have been imported

### What happened
Out of 24 folders and 191 requests, only 21 folders and 169 requests were imported. No errors were reported to indicate that the full collection could not be imported. Import file size was ~200KB

The failure was caused by two folders that have the same name at the same folder level in Postman. Postman stores collections as data, whereas Bruno stores collections as a file structure. Since you cannot have two folders at the same directory level with the same name, the import of that second folder fails. However, this is done without any notification to the user.

There should be a check during the import of a folder to ensure that the folder does not exist. If it does, either notify the user or, possibly better, add a number to the end of the folder so that the import can be successfully continued. The user should be notified of this so that they can then go in and clean up the second folder as needed.

title: fix(openapi-import): root security should be optional
body:
# Description

<!-- Explain here the changes your PR introduces and text to help us understand the context of this change. -->
Learned about Bruno today and tried to import PetStore [openapi](https://petstore3.swagger.io/)
![image](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/assets/632075/5124870b-58fd-41ff-b142-e278b2a3841d)

Basically, it fails to import because the petstore openapi contains `securitySchemes` at root level but no `security` at root level.
The apis `security` are defined on every path.
From the spec (https://swagger.io/docs/specification/authentication/).
```
Step 2. Applying security
After you have defined the security schemes in the securitySchemes section, you can apply them to the whole API or individual operations by adding the security section on the root level or operation level, respectively. When used on the root level, security applies the specified security schemes globally to all API operations, unless overridden on the operation level. In the following example, the API calls can be authenticated using either an API key or OAuth 2. The ApiKeyAuth and OAuth2 names refer to the schemes previously defined in securitySchemes.
```
The root `security` is the default security for every paths and can be overriden at path level, so it is not mandatory.
It fails on this line https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/ba761098be216e802399e8888974377fbe6bbe4b/packages/bruno-app/src/utils/importers/openapi-collection.js#L112
because no `schemes` were returned 
https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/ba761098be216e802399e8888974377fbe6bbe4b/packages/bruno-app/src/utils/importers/openapi-collection.js#L270-L275

Fixes #894

title: Allow variable names to begin with a digit
body:
### Background
Recently we enforced strict validation on variable names in https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/issues/682

Rules
* A variable name must start with a letter or _
* A variable name cannot start with a digit
* A variable name can only contain alpha-numeric characters, `_` or `-`

The reasoning was
* In the future, we want to support special variables `$` Ex: `$randomName`, `$randomEmail` etc. So enforcing some strictness early on made sense
* Its also good to nudge users to adhere to Javsacript variable naming rules since Bruno has powerful scripting capabilities

### Problem Description
Some of users would still like the option to allow a variable name with a digit.

### Solution
I don't think we should change our strict validation since this might only be needed for a smaller audience.
And as a project, we also don't want to take a hard stance on variable naming strictness. I would like us to be flexible and allow overrides on the default behaviour.

I am thinking of supporting an additional config in `bruno.json`
```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "allowVarNameToStartWithDigit": true
  }
}
```

Looking for feedback.

cc @Its-treason @martinsefcik @mirkogolze

title: White screen on environment variables page after setting numeric value with bru.setEnvVar
body:
### Description
There seems to be an issue with the Bruno REST client where storing a numeric value using the `bru.setEnvVar` function causes the Environment Variables overview page to fail to load. The page stays blank until Bruno is restarted. However, when storing a numeric value as a string, this issue does not occur.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Go to the Script section under Post Response.
2. Execute the following line of code to set a numeric value:
   `bru.setEnvVar("locationId", 123);`
3. Attempt to open the Environment Variables overview page - the issue occurs, the page stays white.
4. Restart Bruno REST client, repeat step 1.
5. Execute the following line of code to set a numeric value as a string:
   `bru.setEnvVar("locationId", String(123));`
6. Attempt to open the Environment Variables overview page again - this time, the issue does not occur, and the page loads correctly.

### Expected Behavior
The Environment Variables overview page should open without issues, showing the list of variables, regardless of whether the value set is numeric or a string.

### Actual Behavior
When a numeric value is set with `bru.setEnvVar("locationId", 123);`, the Environment Variables overview page does not load and remains blank. Only after restarting the Bruno REST client does the page become accessible again. Conversely, setting the value as a string with `bru.setEnvVar("locationId", String(123));` does not lead to this issue.

### Additional Information
- Bruno REST client version: v1.1.0 (AppImage)
- Operating System: Linux Mint

The issue appears to be specific to setting numeric values directly. I have not encountered this problem when setting strings or booleans.

Any assistance in resolving this would be greatly appreciated.

title: [Feature] Add JSONPath response filtering
body:
# Description

Adds an input at the bottom of the response where you can enter JSONPath expressions (https://goessner.net/articles/JsonPath/)

Example URL : https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts

Example JSONPath expression :

title: [Feature-Request] request-level environment variables
body:
Hi, is it possible to specify variables for the URL at the level of a request environment? We would like to start using Bruno in the team, if we customize IDs in REST URIs, which is the rule, then they should not be updated in the `.bru`, but rather be quickly replaceable as request-level environment variables.

Sorry if this already exists in the documentation or as an issue, I searched both for a long time but found nothing specific.

**Edit**, 2023-11-10:
As I haven't heard anything about this, I assume it doesn't exist yet, so I've turned it into a feature request.

What does not work at the moment?
=> Quick and easy management of environment variables at the request level, without writing them to a `.bru` file.

How might this feature be implemented?
- Handle request level environment variables like normal variables, i.e. simply using {{var_name}}
- Request-level environment variables **override** global variables.
- They could be placed in the Vars tab like pre- and post-request variables.
- Unlike pre- and post-request variables, they are not synchronised in the `.bru` file, but behave like global **secret environment variables**. 

Unfortunately I only have a basic knowledge of Electron, I work more in the Go & PHP backend. If I have the time, I can try to submit a merge request, but I doubt it will be implemented correctly or "nicely". Maybe someone else here has more skills than me.

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
```

title: [BUG] cURL schema validation gets triggered when adding HTTP Request
body:
When trying to add an HTTP Request, the cURL Command validation get's triggered blocking the form from submitting.
This bug is due to the `formik.touched` getting as `true` as all the fields are part of same form and the schema validation is not conditional.

This fix adds a conditional schema in Yup so that the schema validation for **From cURL** occurs only when the user has selected the **From cURL** option.

title: Can't create environment variable with a "-" in the name
body: I have environments with variable names like `some-service-url`. This has worked in the past. I just upgraded to 1.0.1 and it seems that dashes are not allowed in variable names. Is this intentional or is this a bug? Note that this creates issues when importing a Postman collection (where variable names with dashes _are_ allowed). title: Calling setEnvVar without converting response value to string results in crash when configuring environment
body:
**Version:** 1.0.0

A "crash" seems to be caused when using `setEnvVar` to set an environment variable to a response value which is not a string. This only seems to happen when setting equal to a value from the response. If using `setEnvVar("value", 123456789)` directly it works fine, but if `123456789` is part of the response-object it seems to not handle it correctly.

## Example
Given the following response from an API:
```json
{
  "value": 123456789,
}
```

The following script will cause a crash when clicking to configure environment:
```ts
const body = res.getBody()
bru.setEnvVar("value", body.value);
```

The following script will fill in the value as expected:
```ts
const body = res.getBody();
bru.setEnvVar("value", `${body.value}`)
```
